panels.rationale: Single-panel dermoscopic image from a study on dermoscopy in pityriasis alba among children; the caption explicitly labels the hypopigmented structureless area, fine scaling and ill-defined borders, all of which are recognized dermoscopic features of pityriasis alba and match the provided vocabulary. The caption calls the image 'typical', supporting classic typicality.
panels.attribution_text: Thomas et al. Usage of Dermoscopy as an Effective Diagnostic Tool in Pityriasis Alba: A Prospective Observational Study Among Children in a Suburban Hospital in South India.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.40271. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Typical dermoscopic image showing four distinct patterns The image shows a white structureless area (black arrow), scaling (black star), ill-defined borders (red arrow), and pigmented hairs (red arrow).
in_text_mentions: Typically, Pityriasis alba progresses through a series of stages, starting with an early papular stage, followed by a hypopigmented patch with fine surface scales, and finally resolving as post-inflammatory hypopigmented, non-scaly macules [7]. Four distinct dermoscopy image patterns of scaling, hypopigmented structureless areas, normal hair colour, and indistinct borders were consistently observed in all of the examined patches (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: An 8-year-old child with three hypopigmented scaly patches
An 8-year-old child with three hypopigmented scaly patches (facial photographs)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Clinical photograph of a child with three hypopigmented, faintly scaly facial patches, matching the article's focus on pityriasis alba in children; caption explicitly describes the lesions as hypopigmented scaly patches. B: Dermoscopic image paired with clinical panel A of the same patient with pityriasis alba; caption explicitly documents white structureless areas and indistinct borders. Skin tone not reliably assessable under dermoscopic illumination. C: Clinical photograph of a 6-year-old child with multiple hypopigmented, faintly scaly patches on the cheek, consistent with pityriasis alba as described in the caption and article. D: Dermoscopic image paired with clinical panel C of the same child with pityriasis alba; caption documents white structureless areas and indistinct borders. E: Clinical photograph of a 6-year-old child with multiple hypopigmented, faintly scaly patches on the cheek, consistent with pityriasis alba....
